title: Scissors
prompt: a pair of scissors holding a strip of paper on a table with three buttons: “Open” separates the blades; “Cut” closes the handles and shears the paper; “Move paper” places it nearer the pivot to increase cutting force; see-through reveals the pivot and overlapping wedge-shaped cutting edges
blurb: A teaching adaptation of paired levers and wedge-shaped edges that shear paper with more force near the pivot.

adaptation.initialState: Closed blades with a completed snip. Reset supplies fresh paper and opens the blades.
adaptation.geometry: Generic scissors enlarged for legibility; paper and bevel thickness exaggerated. No exact book artwork reproduction.
adaptation.force: Ideal per-blade force from a 10 N perpendicular effort at a 65 mm handle arm. Load arm changes from 70 to 34 mm. Omits blade friction, flex, grip angle, fracture toughness and force fluctuations.
adaptation.movePaper: Opens before sliding; preserves existing cuts. Reset replaces the specimen as a teaching action.

sources.title: The Way Things Work Now, printed page 14
Mahvash et al. Modeling the Forces of Cutting with Scissors, 2008
sources.supports: Shared pivot, blade contact and fracture; handle force relates to cutting torque and contact distance. Real forces include friction and fracture.

verification.productionTelemetry: n/a, standalone static HTML with no installed production telemetry
